tasks.commitBody:
A signed file URL lives 60 seconds and must never be cached — Entu's own rule, quoted at the signing site — so the only thing that can survive a rehearsal with no signal is the bytes. Opening a part now reads through an identity-partitioned byte store: hit serves stored bytes as a blob URL; miss mints a fresh signed URL, fetches, stores, serves. The signed URL itself is never persisted, and the popup-blocker-safe synchronous tab-open survives in all three handlers (agenda, event, library — the event page also gains the error surface it never had; zero new locale strings).

Staleness is structural, probe-settled on polyphony (ledgers cited at the site): no Entu replace path ever lets the same file-property _id serve different bytes, so keying on the _id makes a replaced file an automatic miss with no validator logic. Partitioning follows the PO ruling on the issue: keys are (database, person-id, file-id) captured at request-issue time, an anonymous session can construct no key, and the store is RETAINED across logout by keeping it out of the auth teardown entirely; the partition is stated in code as a correctness boundary, not a security one; clearPartition ships now, its member-facing control belongs to #334. The cap is global with least-recently-opened eviction. fake-indexeddb enters devDependencies for the adapter tests (approved on-issue); runtime dependencies remain zero.

The review round hardened the principle the PO named: the cache must never prevent a file from opening. The cap is decided before buffering — an over-cap file skips the store and the tab gets the signed URL it already holds, the pre-store delivery path — and a byte fetch that rejects (the CORS shape dev and previews hit while the bucket allowlist covers only production) falls back to the same navigation rather than a closed tab. Every open reports which path delivered — cache, stored, uncached, or fallback — because the availability work on #334 must never mistake a degradation for a cache hit; the fallback's site comment says exactly that, and it does not discharge the live infrastructure ask to allowlist the dev and preview origins.

Closes #343

(*MVOX:Palestrina*)
